lifetimeEvidence.criterion: User-approved legal-use benchmark for the country name Nihon/Nippon (Japan) associated with the Taiho code of 701. This is not a proven first adoption year of the name or the first formation of the earlier Yamato polity. The 670 name-change account remains a competing historical interpretation; it is not declared disproven. No mythical founding date, exact month/day, or new geometry is inferred.

sources.title: Imperial Household Agency: 2020 lecture by historian Haruyuki Tono, external exchanges through the missions to Tang
sources.supports: Identifies the Taiho code of 701 as the earliest domestic historical source for the country name and links its adoption with the ritsuryo framework; discusses external recognition associated with the 702 mission.

sources.supports: The Samguk Sagi 670 entry alone does not establish the change year; later compilation and dependence on Chinese historical sources require caution.

sources.supports: Records the Wa-to-Japan name change under December 670; preserved as the competing account rather than silently discarded.
